messages.subject: R-INLA and PARDISO
parts:
I am sorry to announce that collaboration between R-INLA and PARDISO
have come an end. This is due to internal matters within the PARDISO
project only. 

The PARDISO project stopped issuing free academic licenses from the
beginning of this year, and it is unclear if free academic licenses will
return in the future or if it will be commercial license only.
With only commercial license, the PARDISO support in R-INLA will be
faded out at the end of this year. If free academic licenses returns,
the support of PARDISO will be reevaluated at that time.

Existing licenses will still work until expire date.

The current plan is to integrate another modern sparse matrix library
https://people.engr.tamu.edu/davis/suitesparse.html
that is open-source. This migration will take some time. It is actually
a bit of work. We will lose efficiency for huge models compared to
PARDISO, but with the new experimental mode (paper about this is coming
soon on arxiv), this is less of an issue compared to earlier.

Best
Håvard
